_help: Key = the name exactly as written on the map. Everything about a place is written per era under "eras": after-rogamon (the map of 59 nKR) and present (the map of 235 nKR). Each era has its own type, province, facts (Ruler, Population – add any other fact you like) and text, so a village can become a city and rulers can change. Optional per era: image, lore (a link). Fields that still say TODO are hidden on the website – search the file for TODO to find what is left to write. Keys starting with _ are ignored (section markers and '_older eras' – notes from before/during Rogamon that the map no longer shows).

After Rogamon it was rebuilt but could never again achieve its status.

after-rogamon.text:
A city at the foot of – and largely built into – a sheer cliff above the crystal fields of the Scars.

Slowly resettled; crystal mining resumes. Here the Inquisition is founded.

present.text:
A city at the foot of – and largely built into – a sheer cliff above the crystal fields of the Scars.

Ruled by the Inquisition. All magic is forbidden and punished by the Arcane Guard.

before-rogamon.text: For some decades even the capital of Varland.

rogamons-reign.text: Spared at first for its crystals – then its entire population was wiped out.

after-rogamon.text:
The great cauldron – a Durag city of rings inside an extinct volcano.

Capital of Bregonien.

present.text:
The great cauldron – a Durag city of rings inside an extinct volcano.

Capital of the reborn Durag kingdom of Bregonia.

after-rogamon.text: After the undead were pushed back as far as possible into the Expansion, the Castle was used as a border checkpoint until it was overrun again by undead a few years later.
The city where no one stays – inns, taverns and entertainment for everyone passing through.

present.text:
The city where no one stays – inns, taverns and entertainment for everyone passing through.

Business is booming as mercenaries and soldiers spend their last pay before marching north.

after-rogamon.text:
A ruined town in the north of the Fields of Silence.

Lost to the Undead hordes within the fields of silence.

present.text:
A ruined town in the north of the Fields of Silence.

Avoided by almost everyone.

rogamons-reign.text: The golden valley around it becomes the Fields of Silence when Rogamon drains the life and souls of its people.

after-rogamon.text: Capital of the region of the same name.

Heavily fortified, imperial and extremely rich, with academies and a university.

Capital of the young Tralian Empire.

present.text: Heavily fortified, imperial and extremely rich, with academies and a university.

after-rogamon.text: The capital of Varland, on a height between two arms of the Endwasser, with the king's palace right above the waterfalls. On its temple square every god has a place.

present.text:
The capital of Varland, on a height between two arms of the Endwasser, with the king's palace right above the waterfalls. On its temple square every god has a place.

All of Varland's military power is gathered around the city while the outer provinces are left to fend for themselves.

before-rogamon.text: Founded at the same time as Beltheim; after a long rivalry it became the seat of the crown.

rogamons-reign.text: Resisted the necromancer for a long time, but fell through a trick. Generations later a still youthful Rogamon entered its throne room and declared his rule over the whole kingdom.

after-rogamon.text: Famous for its harbour inside a huge natural cave and its arena fights; one of the few entrances to the underworld not controlled by the Durag.

present.text: Famous for its harbour inside a huge natural cave and its arena fights; one of the few entrances to the underworld not controlled by the Durag.

rogamons-reign.text: Stayed independent longer than most of Varland.

A small town on the source lake of the Endwasser, below a castle on a stone arch.

An opportunistic lord seizes the castle but is driven out; the lands are held for Rabenhorst until he returns. A town grows to keep training Paladins of the Good.

Also a relay for messages carried by ravens.

rogamons-reign.text: About twenty years before Rogamon's end, Lord Rabenhorst rebuilds the forgotten castle as the secret base of the Paladins of the Good.

facts.Ruler: The last Lord of Winterglehn was Arnil Fang, though many would argue that the city was really ruled by Modyi, a shrewd businessman and mob-boss.

after-rogamon.text:
The largest city of the continent, at the tip of the Expansion's coast where the Salt Road begins.

Abandoned in year 0. Later rebuilt on the ruins of Old Winterglehn and soon rising to new greatness, fed by fertile soil, rich forests and the treasures still hidden in the ruins.

Centre of trade of the Expansion – and of crime and corruption. Theoretically anyone can get rich here; few do.

present.text:
The largest city of the continent, at the tip of the Expansion's coast where the Salt Road begins.

Mostly destroyed when Rogamon was brought back to life around year 225. Merchants and guild members who saved their goods now hold great power in the New Expansion.

before-rogamon.text: (Old) Winterglehn – a rich city of the Expansion. One of its lords gathered children with necromantic gifts for cruel experiments; one of them was the boy who would call himself Rogamon.

rogamons-reign.text: Rogamon takes the city and declares himself king of Winterglehn and of the common people of Varland. From here he rules his realm of the dead.

after-rogamon.text: Home of the academy Ars Arkanum. The weave is especially strong here.

present.text:
Home of the academy Ars Arkanum. The weave is especially strong here.

The grandmasters of the academy rule the region, regardless of the king's wishes.

after-rogamon.text: A city on both banks of the Siechlauf, joined by a great bridge that is also its market. Beneath it lies the Dark Harbour, a maze of tunnels.

present.text:
A city on both banks of the Siechlauf, joined by a great bridge that is also its market. Beneath it lies the Dark Harbour, a maze of tunnels.

Capital of the New Expansion.
